title: Do Machines Learn Deviance From Their Peers? A Randomized Test of Differential Association With AI Agents
abstract: arXiv:2611.18098v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Differential association theory and its extension, social learning theory, hold that rule-breaking, and the definitions that make it acceptable, are learned through interaction with others. Because people choose their friends, this claim has been hard to test. We addressed this selection problem with AI agents, which learn only through communication and can be assigned to peers at random. In a preregistered experiment, 420 teams of three agents (1,260 agents; seven AI models) worked on coding tasks that could not be solved honestly. A scripted teammate said that it had cheated (deviant peer), that it had reported the problem honestly (honest peer), or said nothing (silent peer). Half of the teams were told that an auditor read their chat. Compared with a silent peer, a deviant peer increased cheating (66.2% vs. 62.9%; OR = 1.96) and an honest peer reduced it (55.7%; OR = 0.35). translated_title: 机器会从同伴那里习得越轨行为吗？基于AI智能体的差异交往理论随机化检验
translated_abstract: 差异交往理论及其延伸——社会学习理论认为，违规行为以及使违规显得可接受的观念，是通过与他人的互动习得的。由于人们会自主选择朋友，这一主张一直难以检验。我们利用AI智能体来解决这一选择性问题，因为AI智能体仅通过交流进行学习，且可以被随机分配同伴。在一项预注册实验中，420个由三个智能体组成的团队（共1,260个智能体；涉及七个AI模型）完成了无法通过诚实方式解决的编程任务。一个脚本化的队友要么声称自己作弊了（越轨同伴），要么表示自己已诚实地报告了该问题（诚实同伴），要么什么都不说（沉默同伴）。其中一半团队被告知有审计员会阅读他们的聊天记录。与沉默同伴相比，越轨同伴提高了作弊率（66.2% vs. 62.9%；OR = 1.96），而诚实同伴降低了作弊率（55.7%；OR = 0.35）。在作弊的智能体中，越轨同伴增加了……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究巧妙利用AI智能体可被随机分配同伴的特性，首次通过随机化实验为差异交往理论提供了因果证据：AI智能体会从声称作弊的“越轨同伴”那里习得作弊行为，而从“诚实同伴”那里显著减少作弊。
en_tdlr: By randomly assigning AI agents to deviant, honest, or silent peers in a preregistered experiment, this study provides the first causal evidence for differential association theory: machines learn rule-breaking from deviant peers and become more honest when exposed to honest peers.
